correctness.rationale: I checked the Fano-nonline and three-layer graph descriptions by finding an isometry of their distance matrices, without using the supplied isomorphism. A resolving set must meet the separator set for each unordered vertex pair; independent bitset enumeration found zero resolving triples and 7,728 resolving quadruples, and monotonicity excludes smaller sets. Grouping bases by their three-subsets constructs each exchange edge exactly once; the independent count is 155,904 with the entire stated degree histogram. Full distance-preserving backtracking found all 336 graph automorphisms: every surviving branch respects pairwise equality of distances and injectivity, and all choices are exhausted. The 29 resulting base orbits have multiplicities 18×336, 9×168, 2×84. One exact BFS per orbit, weighted by the orbit size and halved for off-diagonal unordered pairs, reproduces the five distance counts, radius, diameter, eccentricity frequencies and all 449,820 detours, including the breakdown by distance. Each exchange can increase intersection with a target by at most one, so the Johnson term is a true lower bound. The explicit bases sharing two landmarks violate the matroid basis-exchange axiom: none of the four target-directed intermediate candidates resolves, and independent BFS gives distance three. The independent group search removes reliance on the cited group order for this census.
residual_risks: Finite result for this 28-vertex graph and arbitrary one-for-one replacements only; no claim for slides or general distance-transitive graphs.

value.rationale: The exchange graph describes how optimal resolving sets on a canonical cubic graph can be reconfigured without using extra landmarks. Among more than 29 million pairs it gives a uniform sharp one-step detour bound, classifies exactly where lengthening occurs by distance, and certifies a non-matroid obstruction. This distinguishes structural behavior not implied by the known dimension or abstract Johnson adjacency, and supplies an exact reference for comparing other graph families.
residual_risks: Does not give a symbolic shortest-path classification or predict arbitrary graph cases.
